title: The Earth as a System and Mining
seo_title: Grade 9 Natural Sciences: The Earth as a System and Mining Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 9 Natural Sciences: The Earth as a system; lithosphere; mining of mineral resources; atmosphere
standard_text: The Earth has four spheres: lithosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere and biosphere. The lithosphere: rocks, minerals and the rock cycle. Mining of mineral resources in South Africa (gold, platinum, coal, diamonds) and its impact. The atmosphere: layers and composition; the greenhouse effect. (summary of CAPS Natural Sciences, Grade 9, Planet Earth and Beyond: The Earth as a system; lithosphere; mining of mineral resources; atmosphere)
meta_desc: Free Grade 9 Natural Sciences worksheets (CAPS): the four spheres, rocks and the rock cycle, mining in South Africa, layers of the atmosphere and the greenhouse effect. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Mining brings wealth but harms land and water.
body_html:
How to think about it

The Earth has four interacting spheres: the lithosphere (rock), hydrosphere (water), atmosphere (air) and biosphere (living things). Rocks are igneous, sedimentary or metamorphic, and change through the rock cycle.

South Africa mines gold (Witwatersrand), platinum (Bushveld), coal (Mpumalanga) and diamonds (Kimberley). Mining creates jobs but can cause acid mine drainage, dust and damaged land. The atmosphere has layers (troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere); greenhouse gases trap heat near the surface.

Example

Which sphere is a river part of?

Water

Answer: the hydrosphere

Example

In which layer of the atmosphere does weather happen?

The lowest layer

Answer: the troposphere

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the spheres work separately.
  • Thinking mining has no environmental cost.
  • Thinking the ozone layer causes the greenhouse effect.

items.q: A volcano erupts and puts ash and gases high into the sky. Which other Earth system is most directly changed, and how?
c: the hydrosphere and biosphere (a lake forms, fish migration is blocked, sediment is trapped)
the atmosphere (cooler temperatures for a year or two)
items.e: A change in one sphere spreads to others.

items.q: Warming thaws permafrost, which releases methane, which causes more warming. What kind of feedback is this?
c: a feedback that only affects rocks
items.e: Positive feedback makes the change bigger; negative feedback makes it smaller.

items.q: Which sphere includes all living things?
items.e: It overlaps with the other three spheres.

items.q: What is a limitation of a box-and-arrow model of the water cycle?
c: it simplifies the system and may leave out how fluxes change over time and place
items.e: Models must be judged by how well they explain data.

items.q: More CO₂ makes some plants grow faster and take up more CO₂. What kind of feedback is this?
items.e: It partly offsets the rise in CO₂.

items.q: More prey lets predators increase, and the predators then reduce the prey. What kind of feedback is this?
c: a feedback that only affects rocks
items.e: Positive feedback makes the change bigger; negative feedback makes it smaller.

items.q: Which four spheres make up the Earth system model?
c: crust, mantle, outer core and inner core
items.e: Matter and energy move between the spheres.

items.q: A city paves over a large area. Which other Earth system is most directly changed, and how?
c: the atmosphere (cooler temperatures for a year or two)
items.e: A change in one sphere spreads to others.

items.q: What is a reservoir (store) in an Earth system model?
c: a place where matter is held for a time, such as the ocean or the atmosphere
items.e: Fluxes move matter between reservoirs.

items.q: Why do scientists use models of Earth systems?
c: because models are always exactly right
to simplify complex systems so they can be explained and predictions tested
items.e: All models have limitations.

items.q: Rain falling on a mountain wears away rock and carries sediment to the sea. Which spheres interact?
items.e: Weathering and erosion link the spheres.

items.q: Warmer oceans evaporate more water, and water vapour is a greenhouse gas that causes more warming. What kind of feedback is this?
c: a closed loop with no effect
items.e: The water vapour feedback amplifies warming.

items.q: Warmer air holds more water vapour, a greenhouse gas, which causes more warming. What kind of feedback is this?
c: a feedback that only affects rocks
items.e: Positive feedback makes the change bigger; negative feedback makes it smaller.

items.q: More CO₂ helps some plants grow faster, and they take more CO₂ out of the air. What kind of feedback is this?
c: a feedback that only affects rocks
items.e: Positive feedback makes the change bigger; negative feedback makes it smaller.

items.q: Glaciers melt quickly in a warm period. Which other Earth system is most directly changed, and how?
c: the atmosphere (cooler temperatures for a year or two)
the geosphere and hydrosphere (coasts erode faster without reefs)
the hydrosphere and biosphere (a lake forms, fish migration is blocked, sediment is trapped)
items.e: A change in one sphere spreads to others.

items.q: What is a flux in an Earth system model?
c: the rate at which matter or energy moves between reservoirs
items.e: Evaporation is a flux from ocean to atmosphere.

items.q: A bushfire burns a forest. Which spheres are affected?
c: all four: the biosphere burns, smoke enters the atmosphere, soils are exposed and runoff changes
items.e: Disturbances spread through the system.

items.q: A hotter Earth gives off more infrared energy to space, which cools it down. What kind of feedback is this?
c: a feedback that only affects rocks
items.e: Positive feedback makes the change bigger; negative feedback makes it smaller.

items.q: What is residence time?
c: the time a river takes to reach the sea
the average time matter stays in a reservoir
items.e: Water stays in the atmosphere for about 9 days but in deep groundwater for thousands of years.

items.q: Which sphere includes all of Earth's water, including ice and groundwater?
items.e: Ice is sometimes called the cryosphere.

items.q: Natural factor: Large deposits of coal and iron ore. How did this influence human activity?

Early farming villages grew along the Nile, Tigris and Euphrates rivers.
Steel-making cities grew nearby during the Industrial Revolution.
Farmers settle on the slopes of active volcanoes despite the danger.
items.e: Resources, hazards and climate shape where people live.
